supabase.summary: A backend service that handles database, login, and file storage in one place.
supabase.whyNeeded: For things like sign-up, login, saving posts and comments, or storing uploaded files—Supabase does it for you. You don't need to build a server.

stripe.summary: A payment service used to add card and easy payments to your website.
stripe.whyNeeded: Payments have strict security and legal rules. Using a dedicated service like Stripe is safe and makes it easy to add one-time or subscription payments.

vercel.summary: A hosting service that puts your site on the internet so anyone can visit it.
vercel.whyNeeded: Code alone isn't enough—something has to run it. Vercel does that so you can share your site with a single link.

railway.summary: Hosting that runs your backend server or API on the internet 24/7.
railway.whyNeeded: To keep server code running for data processing, scheduling, or notifications, you need a service like Railway instead of leaving your own computer on.

ga4.summary: Google's visitor analytics tool. See who visited, from where, and which pages.
ga4.whyNeeded: To improve your site you need to know how many people came and where from. GA4 gives you that in a dashboard.

resend.summary: A service for sending email from your website.
resend.whyNeeded: For welcome emails, password reset, or notifications, you need a reliable sender like Resend so your site can send mail automatically.

sentry.summary: A monitoring tool that catches and reports errors on your site.
sentry.whyNeeded: When something breaks, Sentry tells you where and why before users complain, so you can fix it quickly.

sanity.summary: A headless CMS for managing content like text and images. Edits in the admin show on your site.
sanity.whyNeeded: For content you want to change later without a developer—blog posts, landing copy, menu names—edit in Sanity and your site loads it.
